# GAME-SP4.0 — Dedicated artwork and presentation pass

**Agreed:** 15 October 2026, after SP3.0–SP3.3 gameplay was merged into `main`.
**Status:** Planned. **No new artwork is approved or generated by this plan.**
**Gameplay baseline:** `aa1ea5a2ed8df7b1db4bfb89028d9ac81f6b5605` (all three endings implemented).

## Delivery order

1. **SP3.4 lightweight integration gate:** Confirm the three routes, their distinct ending cards, resume/replay and source asset provenance against the merged `main` build. Automated branch checks were green at merge; actual full browser playthrough and timing remain to be performed. Catalogue defects rather than expanding gameplay now.
2. **SP4.0 consistent art pass:** Create and individually approve missing backgrounds, scene-specific character poses, foreground puzzle props, reveal effects and end-card imagery. Use versioned manifests in the existing Google Drive/OIDC pipeline; never paint interactive text, speech bubbles or buttons into background artwork.
3. **SP4.1 polish and limited expansion:** Once all new art is integrated, undertake cross-route tidy-up, responsive UI and accessibility fixes, text/voice pacing, sound polish and only a small number of owner-approved additions. No broad rewrite, new storyline or fourth route. Re-check the whole game and the **15–25-minute** first-play target.

## Creative and technical art rules

- Reuse the approved Stephen, David and Paul model sheets, expression/crop sets and provenance. Do not fabricate unrelated replacements.
- Design shared aspect ratios/vanishing points and a consistent painted/comic visual language across route scenes. Distinguish props/background/actors, retain responsive placement in CSS, and preserve clickable hit targets.
- Generated image sources should go to the dedicated Drive staging folder, reviewed individually and materialised only via `generated-assets/manifests/` into public WebP on a short-lived branch. No keys, tracking, external image links or original source dumps in Git.
- All events are exaggerated adult fiction; avoid real logos, legal agencies, national insignia, identifiable employers/third parties and graphic anatomy.
- Scene and prop illustrations are separate from UI. Text remains crisp, localisable and accessible. No screen should depend on decoding tiny text baked into an illustration.
- Keep the functional three-route branches merged and stable; artwork can be applied incrementally without merging unfinished combinations.

## Prioritised illustration inventory

### Shared rescue scenes

- Review the existing **hotel lobby** backdrop and separately approved David/Paul standing cut-outs; reuse unless a particular composition needs adjustment, rather than regenerating approved art.
- Align framing, lighting, character size and interactive UI styling at the common route briefing, puzzle and ending shells.
- Give three ending cards a consistent treatment with the appropriate route-specific image.

### Route A — The Summit

- Entrance / mountain club environment with a fictional gatekeeper.
- Approved poses for the gatekeeper, David/Paul where needed, and Stephen happily seated in casual holiday clothes wearing the `TEMPORARY SUPREME CHAIRMAN` sash.
- Three distinct visual card/object props: charger, compliment and flight-notice motifs.
- Grandiose throne-room finishing illustration and a simple stinger for David failing the humility application.

### Route B — The Great Stamp Catastrophe

- Clearly imaginary **Office of Ceremonial Misunderstandings** counter, piles of forms, non-identifiable fictional official, printer and separate waiting-room beat with unharmed Stephen.
- Distinct fictional bear-document illustration, Paul’s takeaway cup, removable APPROVED stamp, readable but separately rendered permit.
- Silly paper/confetti flourish, final departure illustration and framed `PLEASE LEAVE` certificate gag.

### Route C — Reassemble Stephen Martin

- **Total Renewal Spa** and adjacent fake promotional-display workshop as stylised, safe comedy environments.
- One coherent illustrated *cardboard/foam cut-out* model and separate transparent six parts matching the already fixed DOM slot IDs (head, torso, two arms, two legs).
- Cartoon extra pieces: three spare kidneys, Wi-Fi heart, toaster, plastic banana and mystery foam spleen; visually obvious harmless props, not anatomical gore.
- Model power-up LED/light flourish, reveal of unharmed Stephen in a spa robe holding cucumber slices, speaking cardboard mannequin and David’s triumphant final pose.

## Production sequencing and acceptance

Create a brief visual bible/moodboard once, then approve each artwork set independently in this order: (1) location backgrounds, (2) character poses/expressions, (3) separate interactive props, (4) reveal transitions and ending illustrations. Build a playable branch preview after every coherent set; user reviews screenshots in laptop and tablet aspect ratios and approves before merge.

**Do not** change dialogue, puzzle rules, 3-route canon or save-state formats as side-effects of adding art. Record technical defects in a small backlog for SP4.1 unless they block art composition. A final run-through should verify pointer/touch/keyboard controls, scene layers, save/replay, full narrative timing, accessibility and public-release privacy review.

## Proposed first review

Start with the **Summit** entrance and throne-room visual direction, since SP3.1 is the first route-specific ending; only generate a particular artwork asset after its scope, perspective and character references are settled with the owner.
